questions.question: Who issues Central Government Securities in India?
options: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Government of India
questions.explanation: RBI conducts debt management operations and auctions for the Government of India.

questions.question: How often do most dated Government of India bonds pay interest (coupons)?
questions.explanation: Standard dated G-Secs pay coupon interest semi-annually (every 6 months) directly to the bondholder's account.

questions.question: What is the standard face value of a Government of India bond?
questions.explanation: Government bonds have a standard face value of ₹100 per unit.

questions.question: If prevailing market interest rates increase, what happens to the market resale price of an existing fixed-rate G-Sec?
options: Its price stays exactly unchanged forever
questions.explanation: Bond prices have an inverse relationship with interest rates. When interest rates rise, existing bonds with lower coupons drop in price.

questions.question: Where can a retail individual buy G-Secs directly from the RBI with zero brokerage?
options: At a local post office counter only
Via the RBI Retail Direct portal (rbiretaildirect.org.in)
questions.explanation: The RBI Retail Direct scheme allows individual retail investors to open a free Gilt account and participate directly in primary government bond auctions.
